**Severity:** warning · **Area:** Syntax / JSX / attributes (`RV1xxx`) · **Quick fix:** yes

## Message

The diagnostic reads one of:

```text
`{name}` is read and written in an effect: the read subscribes the effect to its own write, so it re-runs until the 10000-run cutoff. Use `{name}.update((v) => …)`: it reads without subscribing
```

```text
`{name}` is read and written in a computed: the read subscribes the computed to its own write, and signal writes throw during computed evaluation. Derive the value instead, or write it from an effect or handler with `{name}.update((v) => …)`
```

Parts in braces (`{name}`) are filled in for each report.

## How to fix

In an effect, write from the current value with update, which reads it untracked: `count.update((v) => v + 1)` instead of `count.set(count() + 1)`. In a computed, do not write at all: derive the value (`computed(() => count() + 1)`) or move the write into an effect or handler.

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
import { effect, signal } from "@rivetjs/reactivity";
const items = signal<string[]>([]);
const incoming = signal("");
effect(() => {
  if (incoming()) items.set([...items(), incoming()]);
});
```

```tsx prefer
import { effect, signal } from "@rivetjs/reactivity";
const items = signal<string[]>([]);
const incoming = signal("");
effect(() => {
  const next = incoming();
  if (next) items.update((v) => [...v, next]);
});
```

## Quick fix

The [language service](../guides/tooling/language-service.md) (editor) and the MCP `check_code` tool offer this code action:

- Read untracked: `x.update((v) => …)` → `x.set(<expr>) becomes x.update((v) => <expr with each direct x() replaced by v>) (effects only)`

## When it is reported

Language service only (editor, rivet check); warning; TS-side, type-aware (the receiver's type is the @rivetjs/reactivity Signal; stores have another API). Fires only where the scope is provably tracked: the inline, non-async function of effect / computed (@rivetjs/reactivity) or clientEffect (@rivetjs/runtime/dom), including `batch(() => …)` bodies inside it. Silent in event handlers, on\* props, callbacks, untrack bodies, JSX and component bodies (components run untracked): there `x.set(x() + 1)` is the faster form (update allocates a closure and swaps the observer; an untracked read returns early).
